instruction: Since I started caring for my mother, my friends have stopped inviting me to things. I know they may think I am too busy, but it still hurts. I don't know how to tell them I miss them.
My family is around, but I feel completely alone in caregiving. Everyone talks to me about what needs to be done, but no one asks how I am doing. I don't know how to explain this feeling.
I keep cancelling plans because I never know when my father will need me. Eventually people stop asking. I want to reconnect, but I feel embarrassed about how often I have cancelled before.

My partner says I have no time for our relationship anymore because all my attention goes to my mother. I feel defensive because I am doing my best, but I can see that we are drifting apart. What could I do?
I feel resentful when I see friends going on holidays or enjoying weekends while I am stuck managing caregiving. Then I feel guilty for being jealous. I don't like how bitter I am becoming.
My friends keep saying things like 'just put your mother in a home' or 'you need to get out more.' They don't understand our situation, and I have started avoiding them. How should I handle this?

I would like to see someone or have a conversation that isn't about caregiving, but every day is full of tasks. By the time I have free time, I am too exhausted to do anything. Can you suggest something realistic?
People ask how caregiving is going, and I always say 'fine' because I don't want to burden anyone. Honestly, it is not fine. I don't know how to open up without feeling like I am complaining.
My sister and I used to be close, but caregiving has turned every conversation into an argument about who is doing more. I miss our relationship and don't know how to get past the resentment.
When I meet people, they ask about my father but never about me. I feel like I have disappeared into the caregiver role. I miss being seen as a person with my own interests and life.
A close friend thinks I am exaggerating how demanding caregiving is because she has never experienced it. I am tired of trying to explain and feel like our friendship may be changing.
I would love to go out for coffee with a friend, but I feel anxious leaving my father even for an hour. I know I need connection, but I can't relax when I am away from him.

I went to a family gathering and everyone seemed to be enjoying their lives normally. I spent the whole time thinking about what I had to do at home and felt sad and disconnected. I don't know why it affected me so much.
I finally asked a friend if she could spend some time with me, and she was busy. I know she has her own life, but I felt rejected and now I don't want to ask anyone else.
I used to be someone who enjoyed travel, hobbies, and meeting people. Now almost every conversation and decision revolves around caregiving. I worry that I don't know who I am anymore.

My friends talk about work, holidays, and ordinary problems, and I feel disconnected because caregiving occupies my entire mind. I don't want to make every conversation about my situation, but I struggle to relate.
My partner wants us to go out and socialize more, but I have no energy and worry about leaving my mother. We keep arguing about it, and neither of us feels understood.

I moved closer to my father to care for him and left most of my friends behind. I don't know anyone in this area, and it feels difficult to start building a social life while caregiving takes so much of my time.
The daytime is busy with caregiving tasks, but at night I feel very lonely. I have no one I feel comfortable calling, and sometimes the silence makes everything feel heavier. What might help?
I know I need to reconnect with people, but I cannot commit to clubs, regular events, or anything that adds pressure. I want something small and manageable that helps me feel less isolated.
